items.X_desc: Score 10 if the abstract pairs a formal/theoretical result with a matching empirical validation of that same claim. Score 0 if the abstract is purely theoretical with no empirical check, or purely empirical with no theoretical grounding for the claim made.
items.Y_desc: Score 10 when each major claim is paired with concrete tasks, data regimes, comparisons, metrics, and conditions; score 0 when the abstract relies mainly on superlatives, benchmark names, or generic assertions.

items.X_desc: Score 10 when the central idea is stated at a level that naturally maps across tasks or domains and the abstract explains those mappings; score 0 when the contribution is inseparable from one benchmark and has no reusable abstraction.
items.Y_name: Novel Problem Formulation Together with Infrastructure
items.Y_desc: Score 0 if the abstract tackles a heavily studied, standard benchmark task. Score 10 if it formalizes a completely new problem space that connects previously disjoint domains, and provides the necessary infrastructure (datasets, simulators) to explore it.

items.X_desc: Score 10 when experiments are structured to distinguish mechanism, scope, and alternatives through matched baselines, ablations, and varied conditions; score 0 when the abstract offers only a single benchmark comparison.
items.Y_desc: Score 10 when the abstract clearly states when the method works, fails, or changes behavior, including relevant data or parameter conditions; score 0 when it makes unqualified claims.

items.X_desc: Score 10 when the abstract identifies a concrete failure mechanism and an intervention that directly addresses it; score 0 when it merely pairs a generic problem with a generic method.
items.Y_name: Fine-Grained Failure Analysis Together with Targeted Mitigation
items.Y_desc: Score 0 if the abstract vaguely claims prior work is 'suboptimal' or 'slow'. Score 10 if it pinpoints the exact mathematical, architectural, or structural bottleneck of prior methods and proposes a solution specifically architected to bypass that exact bottleneck.

items.X_name: Names the causal mechanism behind a known failure
items.X_desc: Score 10 if the abstract identifies WHY an existing phenomenon or failure occurs — a specific mechanism, and then derives the fix from that mechanism. Score 5 if a mechanism is gestured at but the method is not visibly derived from it. Score 0 if the abstract only reports that a method works better, with the cause of the prior failure unexamined.
items.Y_name: Self-aware disclosure of limitations or failure modes
items.Y_desc: Score 10 if the abstract itself names a concrete limitation, negative result, or scenario where the method fails/was later beaten, without being prompted. Score 0 if the abstract is uniformly self-promotional with no caveat.

items.X_desc: Score 10 when the abstract clearly states when the method works, fails, or changes behavior, including relevant data or parameter conditions; score 0 when it makes unqualified claims.

items.X_name: Robustness or generality is demonstrated across regimes, not one setting
items.X_desc: 10 = the same fixed method is shown to hold across genuinely different task families, scales, or conditions, with sameness of configuration made explicit. 5 = several datasets from one family. 0 = a single benchmark, or many benchmarks that differ only cosmetically.

items.X_name: Reports a limitation or negative result against own claim

anchors.X_name: Presence of a trailing signature block
anchors.X_desc: Score 0-10 for how fully the text ends with a personal sign-off: a name, initials, a handle, or a closing salutation. Extent only.
anchors.Y_name: Author sign-off at the end of the text
anchors.Y_desc: Score 0-10 for whether the writer closes by naming or initialling themselves. Extent only; do not judge quality.

anchors.X_name: How much displayed mathematics the text contains
anchors.X_desc: Score 0-10 for the density of set-off equation blocks. Count only; do not judge whether the mathematics is correct.
anchors.Y_name: How much the text hedges its own claims
anchors.Y_desc: Score 0-10 for the frequency of 'I think', 'perhaps', 'it seems' and similar. Count only; do not judge whether the hedging is warranted.
